dashboard.guided.title: Guided test drive (optional)
dashboard.guided.hint: Three short steps that let the report tell a vibration that follows road speed from one that follows the engine. Only do them where it is safe.
dashboard.guided.sweep.title: Speed sweep
dashboard.guided.sweep.instruction: In top gear (or D), accelerate smoothly from about {from} to {to} {unit}, or as high as is safe and legal. Without OBD-II, the engine check assumes top gear.
dashboard.guided.hold.title: Steady hold
dashboard.guided.hold.instruction: Still in top gear (or D), hold a steady speed where you feel the vibration most, for about 20 seconds.
dashboard.guided.coast_down.title: Neutral coast-down
dashboard.guided.coast_down.instruction: At that speed, shift to neutral and let the car roll about {drop} {unit} slower without braking. Then shift back into gear.
dashboard.guided.done: Guided test done. Stop the recording when you're ready.

history.confidence_meaning.weak: don't buy parts; record the test again
history.verdict.weak_evidence: Not enough evidence to name a cause
history.verdict.weak_body: Best candidate: {source} ({location}). Don't buy parts on this alone.
history.verdict.no_fault_body: Nothing stood out in the checks this run could make: {checked}.
history.verdict.no_fault_nothing_checked: No vibration stood out, but this run could not check the wheels, driveline or engine against their rhythms, so it does not show that they are fine.
history.verdict.no_fault_not_checked: Not checked, so not shown to be fine: {sources}.
history.checks.ruled_out.wheel_tire: no once- or twice-per-wheel-turn vibration found
history.checks.stayed_in_neutral: ruled out: the vibration kept going while coasting in neutral (it follows road speed)
history.checks.stopped_in_neutral: ruled out: the vibration stopped while coasting in neutral (it follows engine speed)
history.checks.limited.estimated_final_d: checked only against a car-library estimate of the final drive, so not conclusive — enter the exact ratio if you know it.
history.checks.limited.estimated_top_gea: checked only against a car-library estimate of the top-gear ratio, in top gear, so not conclusive — enter the exact ratio if you know it.
history.checks.limited.top_gear_assumed: checked in top gear only: engine RPM was estimated from speed assuming top gear, so lower gears were not checked — an OBD-II adapter measures RPM in every gear.
history.checks.limited.engine_estimated_: checked only against a car-library estimate of the final drive, in top gear, so not conclusive — enter the exact ratio if you know it, or connect an OBD-II adapter to measure RPM.
history.checks.couldnt.no_tire_reference: no tire size — add it to the car in Settings.
history.checks.couldnt.no_drive_referenc: no final-drive ratio — add it to the car in Settings if you know it (optional).
history.checks.couldnt.no_engine_referen: no engine RPM — connect an OBD-II adapter, or add the top-gear ratio to the car (optional).
history.checks.couldnt.manual_speed: the speed was entered by hand, so finding no match proves nothing — record again with GPS or OBD-II speed.
history.checks.couldnt.engine_no_tire_re: no tire size — connect an OBD-II adapter to measure RPM, or add the tire size to the car.
history.checks.couldnt.engine_no_drive_r: no final-drive ratio — connect an OBD-II adapter to measure RPM, or add the final drive and top-gear ratio to the car (optional).
history.checks.hedge.estimated_top_gear: against an estimated top-gear ratio, top gear only
history.checks.hedge.engine_estimated_fi: against an estimated final drive, top gear only

settings.car.top_gear_help: Lets VibeSensor estimate engine RPM from speed when no OBD-II adapter is connected. The estimate assumes you drive in top gear (or D). Leave empty if unknown.

settings.car.estimate.top_gear: Top gear is an estimate for this model family: engine results will be marked as estimated.

settings.sensors.title: Sensors
settings.sensors.hint: Manage sensor names and locations. Default name is the MAC address.
settings.sensors.name: Name
settings.sensors.mounting.title: Where to mount the sensors
settings.sensors.mounting.no_layout: No connected sensor has a location yet.
settings.sensors.mounting.layouts_title: Layouts and what they can tell
settings.sensors.mounting.layout.four_wh: Four wheels plus one in the cabin (best): names the corner or axle of a wheel fault, and the seat sensor shows what you feel.
Four wheels: names the corner or axle of a wheel fault.
settings.sensors.mounting.layout.cabin_o: Cabin only (seat or trunk): tells the source type (wheel, driveline or engine) but cannot name a wheel.
settings.sensors.mounting.layout.single: One sensor anywhere: the source type only, with less certainty.
settings.sensors.mounting.rule.rigid: Mount a wheel sensor on a rigid part near the wheel, such as the steering knuckle or the strut base. Never on the wheel or tire: they rotate.
settings.sensors.mounting.rule.firm: Fix each sensor firmly (a bolt, strong cable ties or a strong magnet). A loose sensor rattles and adds its own vibration.
settings.sensors.mounting.rule.clear: Keep the sensor and its cable clear of moving parts, the brakes and the exhaust.
settings.sensors.mounting.rule.identify: Use Identify to blink a sensor's LED, then pick where it is mounted in the table above.
sensors.layout.single: One sensor: VibeSensor can tell the source type (wheel, driveline or engine) but not where it is.
sensors.layout.no_wheels: No wheel sensors: VibeSensor can tell the source type but cannot name a wheel.
sensors.layout.some_wheels: Sensors at {count} of {total} wheels: a wheel fault can be placed at a corner with a sensor, not on an axle. Add the other wheels to compare corners.
sensors.layout.four_wheels: All four wheels: a wheel fault can be placed at its corner, its axle or all four.

settings.speed.compare.title: What each source can do
settings.speed.compare.gps.hardware: A USB GPS receiver (not included). The Pi 3 A+ has one USB port, which a USB internet connection also uses.
settings.speed.compare.gps.enables: Live speed for the wheel and driveline checks, speed sweeps and the coast-down check.
settings.speed.compare.gps.limits: Engine RPM is estimated from speed, assuming top gear (or D).
settings.speed.compare.obd2.hardware: A Bluetooth ELM327 adapter paired with the Pi. Wi-Fi OBD dongles cannot connect: the Pi's Wi-Fi runs the hotspot.
settings.speed.compare.obd2.enables: Live speed and measured engine RPM, so the engine check needs no gear ratios.
settings.speed.compare.obd2.limits: Needs a fresh RPM reading from the adapter before you can start.
settings.speed.compare.manual.enables: Only a test held at exactly the speed you enter.
settings.speed.compare.manual.limits: No speed sweep, amplitude-vs-speed or coast-down check. Every sample is treated as being at the set speed, so results are hedged.

settings.update.journey_intro: The updater works through these stages in order, so the current step and what comes next stay visible on one screen.

settings.esp_flash.recovery.summary_retr: The last flash stopped before completion. Review the captured details, then retry when the board is ready.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.summary_bloc: The last flash stopped before completion. Reconnect the board and clear the blocked item before retrying.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.item.next_st: Reconnect the board over USB and refresh the port list before retrying the flash.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.fallback_err: The flash stopped before it could report a detailed error.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.validating.d: Confirm the selected board or auto-detected port is correct, then retry the flash.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.preparing.ti: Fix the build or bundle problem
settings.esp_flash.recovery.preparing.de: Review the live output and resolve the firmware bundle or toolchain problem before retrying.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.erasing.deta: Keep the ESP board powered, reconnect USB if needed, and retry only when the connection stays stable.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.flashing.det: Reconnect the board, confirm the selected port, and retry once the cable and power are stable.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.cancelled.de: Review the selected target and any live output, then start a new flash only when the board is ready.
settings.esp_flash.recovery.generic.deta: Use the failed step, recent attempt, and log output below to understand the problem before retrying.
settings.esp_flash.history_intro: Recent flashes stay here so the next operator can see what happened last.
settings.esp_flash.journey.detail.valida: Checks that a firmware bundle is available and that the selected board or auto-detected port is usable.
settings.esp_flash.journey.detail.prepar: Loads the cached firmware bundle on the Pi and prepares the flash commands for this board.
settings.esp_flash.journey.detail.erasin: Clears the target flash so the new firmware can be written cleanly.
settings.esp_flash.journey.detail.flashi: Writes the current firmware image over USB and streams the tool output into the live log panel.
settings.esp_flash.journey.detail.done: Stores the outcome and last-success time so the next operator can confirm what happened last.
settings.esp_flash.journey_terminal.fail: The last flash stopped before the remaining stages could finish. Review the error, log output, and latest attempt before trying again.
settings.esp_flash.journey_terminal.canc: The last flash was cancelled before the remaining stages could finish. Confirm the selected target and restart only when the board is ready.
settings.esp_flash.readiness.summary.rea: The Pi can see at least one serial device. Confirm the target and start when the board is ready.
No serial device is detected yet. Connect the ESP32 by USB and refresh before starting.
settings.esp_flash.readiness.summary.run: Flashing is in progress. Keep the board powered and connected until the status returns.
settings.esp_flash.readiness.summary.suc: The most recent flash completed successfully. You can review the last result and flash again if needed.
settings.esp_flash.readiness.summary.fai: The last flash ended with an error. Review the last attempt and logs before trying again.
settings.esp_flash.readiness.summary.can: The last flash was cancelled. Review the current port selection before starting again.
settings.esp_flash.logs_intro: Build, erase, and upload output appears here while the toolchain runs.
settings.esp_flash.logs_failed_body: Use the failed step and recent-attempt details below to recover, then retry once the board is ready.
settings.esp_flash.logs_idle_body: Start a flash to stream tool output here. If no port is detected yet, reconnect the board and refresh the port list first.
settings.esp_flash.logs_running_body: The job has started. Build and upload output will appear here as soon as the toolchain begins emitting logs.
settings.esp_flash.history_empty_body: Your first successful or failed flash will be recorded here with the target port and result.
settings.wizard.load_failed_hint: The car library is unavailable right now. Try again, go back, or continue with manual specs.
settings.wizard.no_gearboxes: The library has no gearbox data for this car. Enter the ratios below if you know them.
settings.wizard.no_library_data: No library data for {name}: you'll enter the tire size yourself; final drive and top gear are optional.
